target.sector: climate-driven migration and displacement outside coastal CIAM
target.required_output: annual country-level consumption-equivalent welfare difference under matched GIVE baseline and marginal CO2-pulse paths
target.primary_claim: No additive migration SCC is presently authorized

covered_costs: people relocation as a multiple of annual income
coastal_relocation.trigger: coastal dry-land loss under no-adaptation or retreat choices

inland_and_international_migration.status: not represented as an explicit GIVE sector

candidates.title: The Economic Geography of Global Warming
candidates.endpoint: total welfare and spatial economic reallocation with migration as adaptation
failed_gates: non-overlap with GIVE productivity, mortality, energy, agriculture, and amenity pathways

candidates.title: Climate Change, Inequality, and Human Migration
candidates.coverage: global, internal and international migration with skill heterogeneity
candidates.endpoint: migration, inequality, and aggregate climate impacts combining temperature, sea-level rise, disasters, conflict, and productivity
failed_gates: non-overlap with agriculture, conflict, disasters, and productivity

candidates.title: Groundswell climate migration projections
candidates.coverage: scenario-based internal migration to 2050 in covered world regions
failed_gates: separation from water, crop, ecosystem, flood, and sea-level triggers
candidates.disposition: quantity validation only; never multiply by an assumed cost per migrant

candidates.title: Peer-reviewed reduced-form climate/weather and migration studies
candidates.coverage: heterogeneous regional samples and migration definitions
candidates.endpoint: migration probability, net flows, displacement, asylum claims, or post-disaster earnings
candidates.disposition: validation/calibration evidence, not an SCC coefficient

forbidden_shortcuts: GDP loss relabeled as migration welfare
adding total spatial-model climate welfare to existing GIVE damages
treating movement itself as a damage rather than a possible adaptation response
global scaling of a local disaster displacement estimate

next_model_contract.preferred_design: structural spatial-equilibrium sensitivity or replacement, not a default additive sector
next_model_contract.additive_exception: empirically identified real relocation resource costs or nonpecuniary losses incremental to every existing trigger-sector damage
